# HEXACO responses generated by four language models

59,611 synthetic respondents to the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items, generated by
four open-weight large language models for Canada, Great Britain and the
United States, in 10 independent attempts of about 500 respondents per
model and country. They come from a study of how well synthetic
respondents cover real people, and they pair with the real answers in
[hexaco_real](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/hexaco_real.md).

## Usage

``` r
hexaco_llm
```

## Format

A data frame with 59,611 rows (one per synthetic respondent) and 243
columns: `model` (factor, the four models above), `country` (factor:
`Canada`, `Great Britain` or `United States`), `attempt` (1 to 10) and
the 240 items, named as in `hexaco_items$item`.

## Source

Generated for the coverage strip study by Okan Bulut. The script is
`data-raw/hexaco.R` in the package's GitHub repository.

## Details

Each respondent was generated in its own conversation. The model was
asked to simulate one adult drawn at random from the general adult
population of the named country (not an average or typical person), to
answer as that person rather than as an AI or a socially desirable
person, and to use the full range of the scale. No demographic details
were given, so the country was the only part of the prompt that changed.
The items were shown in their original order in six blocks of 40, at
temperature 1.0, between July and September 2026. The models ran on the
Aleph Inference Gateway of the Vulcan cluster (Digital Research Alliance
of Canada):

|               |                                 |           |
|---------------|---------------------------------|-----------|
| `model`       | Checkpoint                      | Developer |
| Gemma 4 26B   | google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (FP8) | Google    |
| GPT-OSS-120B  | openai/gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4)     | OpenAI    |
| Qwen 3.8 27B  | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8            | Alibaba   |
| Qwen 3.5 122B | Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8      | Alibaba   |

379 rows that were logged under another model in the Qwen 3.8 27B files
were removed, so a few Qwen 3.8 27B attempts have fewer than 500
respondents. As in
[hexaco_real](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/hexaco_real.md),
answers are stored as given (1 to 7), with reverse-keyed items not
reversed. No answer is missing.

## See also

[hexaco_real](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/hexaco_real.md),
[hexaco_items](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/hexaco_items.md),
[`synthetic_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/synthetic_coverage.md)
and the article [Checking synthetic
respondents](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/synthetic-coverage.html).

## Examples

``` r
with(hexaco_llm, table(model, country))
#>                country
#> model           Canada Great Britain United States
#>   Gemma 4 26B     5000          5000          5000
#>   GPT-OSS-120B    5000          5000          5000
#>   Qwen 3.8 27B    4945          4995          4671
#>   Qwen 3.5 122B   5000          5000          5000
# one list per model, one data frame per attempt: the shape that
# synthetic_coverage() takes
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada", ]
syn <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model), function(m) split(m[h], m$attempt))
lengths(syn)
#>   Gemma 4 26B  GPT-OSS-120B  Qwen 3.8 27B Qwen 3.5 122B 
#>            10            10            10            10 
```
